blocks.source: Vol IV, Grounded Intent, § Semantic Request Translation to Geometric Proposals
blocks.md: When an operator asks for the red mug and the vision backbone instead binds the word "mug" to an adjacent table fixture, the coordinate that crosses the proposal boundary arrives in the trajectory pipeline indistinguishable from a valid handle target. Low-level motor drives monitor encoder counts, winding temperatures, and phase currents, so they have no way to tell whether the setpoint they track belongs to a mug or a bolted bracket. Any unmodeled arm compliance or thermal expansion also adds metric bias that a high semantic confidence score never reveals.

questions.q: The section **Semantic Request Translation to Geometric Proposals** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Metric precision does not establish identity, so a confident wrong object yields a collision-free, torque-limited proposal that passes every check the safety MCU can make, and semantic errors need their own defense.

A conformal predictor returns a set of candidate answers whose threshold is calibrated on held-out labeled cases, keeping every candidate it cannot exclude and giving a chosen coverage rate under exchangeability.
Task and motion planning certifies symbolic facts with geometric samplers, whether a classical planner or a language model wrote the plan.
Phantom, stale, ambiguous, misclassified, and dynamically unreachable targets all arrive in the same well-formed wire format, so each needs its own detector.
